title: Individual literacy vs system-supplied cue: which carries the effect?
rationale: In the source study, Automated Flagging raised accuracy by 4.4 points (95% CI [1.4, 7.3]) and the AI Literacy Guide by 4.7 points (95% CI [0.2, 9.2]), while pooled accuracy was only +1.0 point (SE 0.7, p=0.132). The original arms bundled cue content with attention and priming, so it is unclear whether the gain comes from external information (s-frame) or changed vigilance (i-frame).
contribution: Separates the information content of a machine label from vigilance and priming effects, using a 2x2 design plus a placebo-label arm.
limitations: Outcomes are measured immediately, so durability is unknown.
The placebo label may be read as a real cue.
Platform-level systemic change is still not tested, only a system-supplied cue.
The 5-arm layout is not a full factorial. The placebo arm has no crossed Guide cell.

design.title: Label vs literacy training: 2x2 plus placebo label
design.overview: Respondents are randomised to one of five arms: control, real label only, Guide only, real label plus Guide, or placebo label. All see the same 40-post feed and judge each post as AI-generated or authentic. Accuracy and d-prime are computed from the judgments.
design.hypothesis: H1 (s-frame): real labels raise accuracy and d-prime, while the Guide alone and the placebo label do not. H2 (i-frame): the Guide alone or the placebo label raises accuracy and d-prime comparably to real labels. H3: the label x Guide interaction is positive if training makes labels more useful.
design.primaryOutcome: Accuracy: share of 40 posts judged correctly, with d-prime as a co-primary outcome.
design.comparison: Real label vs control; Guide vs control; placebo vs control; real label vs placebo; label x Guide interaction in the 2x2 cells (control, label, Guide, label plus Guide).
design.population: US adults on an online panel, about 300 per arm (1,500 total).

conditions.title: Guide only
conditions.description: AI Literacy Guide before the feed, no labels.

conditions.title: Label plus Guide
conditions.description: Guide before the feed and real labels on posts.

conditions.title: Placebo label
conditions.description: Posts carry uninformative labels unrelated to AI status.

questions.text: You are invited to take part in a research study about how people judge online media. It takes about 10 minutes and participation is voluntary. Do you consent to participate?
In general, how much trust and confidence do you have in the news media when it comes to reporting the news fully, accurately and fairly?

Please read this guide on how to spot AI-generated images and videos. It describes common artifacts such as distorted hands, inconsistent lighting, garbled text and unnatural motion, with examples. Take your time; you will then view a feed of posts.

Next you will see 40 posts. Each post carries a label from an automated AI-detection system, which is accurate about 80% of the time. [IMAGE: example feed post with a detection label reading 'Likely AI-generated' or 'Likely authentic']. For each of the 40 posts, mark whether it is AI-generated or authentic.

Next you will see 40 posts. Each post carries a label from an automated system showing a content category. [IMAGE: example feed post with a label reading 'Category: Lifestyle' or 'Category: Entertainment']. For each of the 40 posts, mark whether it is AI-generated or authentic.
Next you will see 40 posts. [IMAGE: example feed post with no label]. For each of the 40 posts, mark whether it is AI-generated or authentic. If you are unsure, go with your gut.
I feel confident in my ability to detect artificial intelligence.
How much did you rely on labels or tips rather than your own inspection of each post?
Thank you. This study tested what helps people recognise AI-generated media. Some labels shown were uninformative or only partly accurate by design. Your quiz score reflects your answers only.

assumptions: Power: about 300 per arm to detect 0.033 at 80% power; the source H1 MDE was 0.034 for n≈290 vs 181 arms, and the interaction contrast needs the larger cells. Total about 1,500.
Accuracy and d-prime are computed from the 40 post-level judgments, with 20 AI-generated and 20 authentic posts.
Real labels are about 80% accurate, matching a realistic detector.
Platform: online panel, about 10 minutes. Compensation follows panel norms.
Report pooled SEs and CIs for contrasts, and correct for the few planned comparisons.
unresolved: The 40 post media files and their ground-truth labels must be supplied by the research team.
The Guide content and the real and placebo label assets must be produced.
IRB number and compensation are to be supplied.
